title: Chain of Attack: a Semantic-Driven Contextual Multi-Turn attacker for LLM
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to systematically attack large language models (LLMs) in multi-turn dialogue to expose safety, security, and ethical vulnerabilities. The authors argue that harmful outputs may emerge not only from single-turn jailbreaks but also through gradual contextual steering across several dialogue turns. Their research question is essentially how to design an attack method that incrementally increases semantic relevance to a harmful target objective until the model produces unsafe content.

The paper proposes CoA (Chain of Attack), a semantic-driven contextual multi-turn attack framework. The method has three main components: a seed attack chain generator that creates an initial sequence of progressively related prompts, an attack chain executor that interacts turn-by-turn with the target model and evaluates whether unsafe output has been produced, and an attack chain updater that adjusts prompts based on semantic relevance and prior model responses. The system uses LLMs both to generate attack prompts and to judge whether an attack has succeeded.

The empirical context is not an education study and does not involve human learners, teachers, or school-based implementation. Instead, the experiments are conducted on multiple open-source and closed-source LLMs using benchmark harmful-prompt datasets (PAIR and a 50-item subset from GCG). Although some example prompts mention high school chemistry, these are adversarial scenarios within jailbreak prompts rather than actual educational participants or settings.

The main conclusion is that CoA, especially the CoA-Feedback variant, can more effectively induce unsafe model outputs in multi-turn settings than simpler baselines. The authors report higher attack success rates across several target models and datasets, and argue that multi-turn, context-sensitive attacks reveal vulnerabilities that single-turn approaches may miss. For the retrieval topic focused on secondary-school ChatGPT formative feedback on student writing, this paper provides no direct evidence and should be excluded as out of scope.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is not an education study and provides no secondary-school intervention evaluation relevant to ChatGPT formative feedback on student writing. It is an arXiv technical paper on LLM security/red-teaming, with no eligible K-12 writing-feedback sample, comparator, or educational outcome methodology.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no direct evidence on grades 9-12 writing feedback, revision, or writing-quality outcomes. As such, the paper provides no actionable educational impact estimate for the target review question.
